title: Anderson-Rubin Inference for Local Average Treatment Effects with Vanishing Instrument Propensity
banked_reason: D0.5.G assessed a mathematically sound but specialized boundary theorem as incremental below the field floor (paper-score ceiling 5.5 < 7.4; salvageable=false); literature_positioning@thm:uniform-ar-coverage remains unrepaired.
gap_reasons: The note proves a genuine but highly specialized boundary theorem: uniform coverage and random-set limits for one raw clipped-IPW Anderson–Rubin construction under a public linearly vanishing propensity, uniform covariates, exact compliance-shape factorization, and a directional variance floor.

The positive-definite Fieller geometry is prior art, leaving the binary singular-face classification, logarithmic Gaussian approximation, covariance estimator, and endpoint clipping laws as the narrow new content; that package is substantial enough for a specialized venue but not a field-level contribution.

The coverage headline is locally positionable, but its related-work account omits the accepted-bank weak-ratio LATE frontier (stat_transported_late_strength_frontier_v1) and gives no relevance sentence for the cited Staiger--Stock and Mikusheva references; add precise non-subsumption comparisons to complete the theorem-level novelty audit.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery developed a singular-safe clipped-IPW Anderson–Rubin theorem, feasible boundary covariance, and critical and endpoint laws; the typed math referee passed with no mathematical findings. The field-level novelty gate rated the completed note incremental (paper-score ceiling 5.5 below 7.4), and one literature-positioning finding remains. Uniformly valid residualized-score shortening remains an open, out-of-scope augmentation question; no Lean formalization was launched.
tldr: For an observably specified class of binary-instrument propensities that vanish linearly at a boundary, clipping at \(\tau_n=(n\log n)^{-1/2}\) produces the exact variance factor \(\ell_n=\log(n\log n)\) and noise scale \(s_n=\sqrt{\ell_n/n}\). Uniformly over the class with the unchanged compliance lower bound \(\mu_n\ge c\sqrt{\log n/n}\), the paper proves a singular-safe row Gaussian approximation, feasible boundary covariance estimation, and 95 percent coverage for the baseline set \(C_n\), with coverage error \(C\{\mu_n/\ell_n+1/\ell_n+n^{-1/6}\}\), under a variance floor only in tested causal directions. At critical compliance strength, the positive-definite branch is the classical clipped Fieller law, while binary support adds a singular \(\operatorname{diag}(p,0)\) face with deterministic limiting denominator. Measurable clipping and attainable endpoint laws are derived; generic quadratic set classification is credited to Smucler--Lanni--Masip, and uniformly shortening \(C_n\) through nuisance residualization remains open.
gap: Ma's weak-LATE Anderson--Rubin theorem is proved on a fixed-\(\varepsilon\) overlap class; Sasaki--Ura address trimming bias for smooth ratio moments \(\mathbb E[B/A]\); and weak-overlap ATE results of Rothe and Dorn do not provide ratio-score inversion when compliance shrinks and the boundary covariance can be singular.
fill: The project supplies class-uniform Gaussian and covariance approximations, feasible Anderson--Rubin coverage, the binary singular face, measurable clipped boundary laws, and attainable endpoint limits without a full eigenvalue floor; it does not claim a new generic Fieller classification.
